opening.quote: Good morning, thank you for calling Tidewell Home, my name is Sanne.
opening.comment: You greeted the caller and gave your name and the company name in the first turn, which meets the standard.

verification.quote: Can I take your full name and either the order member or the postcode on your account, police?
verification.comment: You asked for full name and order number or postcode, but the caller then gave full name and order number, which satisfies verification before data was shared; the garbled wording was unclear but the check was done.

understanding.quote: So you were charged €49.95 twice for one lamp, and you only want this duplicate payment back, is that right?
understanding.comment: You captured the duplicate charge issue accurately and confirmed the caller's intent without asking for information already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: refunded the duplicate payments of €49.95 today. Your bank will show it within 3 to 5 working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The duplicate refund and 3 to 5 working day timeline match policy, though you said 'duplicate payments' while only one duplicate of €49.95 exists, so the wording should be precise.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: refunded the duplicate payments of €49.95 today.
process_compliance.comment: No hold occurred and no damaged item, bank dispute transfer, or goodwill voucher applied, so no required steps were missed.

communication.quote: I'm sorry about that, being a charged twice is really frustrating.
communication.comment: You acknowledged the caller's annoyance politely and warmly; the closing was courteous as well.

closing.quote: Is there anything else I can help you with?
closing.comment: You confirmed the confirmation email coming and asked if there was anything else before closing politely, which is good practice.
